Where is that Kaca here, according to my word? tam uvāca tataḥ śukraḥ surāpānamadena ca / guruṇā cābhiśāpena bhakṣito 'sau mamātmajaḥ // MatsP_25.35 // Śukra then said to her: "That son of mine was consumed by the drinking of wine and by the curse of his preceptor. tato devayānī kruddhā gurum etad uvāca ha / surāpānena mūḍhasya śāpo 'smai dīyatām iti // MatsP_25.36 // Then Devayānī, filled with anger, said this to her preceptor: "Let a curse be pronounced upon this fool for his drinking of wine. tam uvāca tato bhītaḥ kṛtāñjalir atho guruḥ / na me vācyam anyathā syāt putraḥ prāpto mayā tava // MatsP_25.37 // Thereupon the preceptor, fearing [the king's wrath], spoke with joined palms: "My word cannot be otherwise; your son has been restored by me. devayāny uvāca: yadi putraḥ punar labdho jīvann eṣa mayā guro / surāpānād aduṣṭasya vidhatsva niyamam tv idam // MatsP_25.38 // Devayānī said: "If this son of mine has been recovered alive by me, O Preceptor, then impose this rule upon him who was not guilty of drinking wine: na pātavyā tvayā surā saṃprāpte 'pi svajīvite / na deyaṃ ca tvayā cāsyai duhitre me varaṃ punaḥ // MatsP_25.39 // 'You must not drink wine even at the cost of your own life, nor must you ever again grant a boon to this daughter of mine. evam astv iti taṃ śukraḥ kṛtāñjalir abhāṣata / tato devayānī tuṣṭā babhūva vigatajvarā // MatsP_25.40 // Śukra replied to him with joined palms, "So be it," and Devayānī became satisfied and free from her distress. tatas tu kacam āsādya yathāpūrvaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ / vidyāṃ śikṣayituṃ prāptaḥ śukreṇaiva samanvitaḥ // MatsP_25.41 // Then Kaca, having regained his sight as before, arrived to be taught the sciences, accompanied by Śukra himself. tatas tu devayānī sā pitaraṃ vākyam abravīt / asminn eva vane brahman gā rakṣantu kaco yathā // MatsP_25.42 // Then Devayānī spoke these words to her father: "O Brahmin, let Kaca guard the cows in this very forest as he did before. tatheti coktvā śukreṇa rakṣaṇārthaṃ gavāṃ kacaḥ / punar eva vanaṃ prāptaḥ saha tenaiva bhārgavaḥ // MatsP_25.43 // Having said "So be it," Kaca, the descendant of Bhṛgu, returned to the forest along with Śukra for the purpose of guarding the cows. tatas tu tāḥ samān
"The Agnihotra has been offered by you, O Lord, and the sun has set;
the cows have returned without their herdsman, and Kaca, dear father, is not to be seen."
"O father, it is evident that Kaca must have been killed or captured;
without him I shall certainly not live—I speak the truth. (Matsya Purāṇa 25.35)
Śukra said:
"With the words 'Come here! Come here!', I shall restore the dead to life.
Then, having employed the Saṃjīvanī lore, he called out for Kaca.
Summoned, Kaca appeared and bowed to Śukra;
the son of Dhiṣaṇa then declared, "I have been slain by the Rākṣasas."
Then, addressed by Devayānī, the brahmin Kaca went at his own will to the forest for the purpose of gathering flowers, reciting the eternal Veda.
The Dānavas also saw him gathering flowers in the forest; then,
having slain that peerless one and reduced him to ashes like fine powder,
the Asuras gave it to a Brāhmaṇa in his wine at that time.
Then Devayānī spoke these words once more to her father:
"Father, Kaca, who was sent to fetch flowers, is not to be seen. *Matsya Purāṇa* 25.40.
"O father, it is evident that Kaca must have been killed or has died;
without him I shall certainly not live—I tell you this as the truth. (Matsya Purāṇa 25.41)
Śukra said:
"O daughter, Kaca, the son of Bṛhaspati, has gone to the state of the departed;
though restored to life by my knowledge, he is thus slain again. What shall I do?"

"Do not grieve for him, do not weep, O Devayānī; one such as you should not mourn for a mortal—for you, whose [support] are the sacred knowledge (*brahman*), the Brahmins, the gods led by Indra, the Vasus, and the Aśvins. (Matsya Purāṇa 25.43)
The enemies of the gods and the entire world stood by through the power of my asceticism;
yet this twice-born man, who was restored to life, cannot be brought back to life once he has been slain again.
Devayānī said:

"O Sage, how is it that I do not grieve for him, nor weep, for him whose grandfather was Aṅgiras, the most venerable, and whose father was Bṛhaspati, a treasury of asceticism— him who was the excellent son and now the grandson of a seer?"
He was a celibate student, rich in asceticism, ever-diligent, and indeed skillful in his duties;
I shall follow Kaca’s path and not eat, for dear to me, O father, is the handsome Kaca.
Śaunaka said:
Having been thus addressed by Devayānī, the great seer Kāvya then spoke with indignation:
"Without a doubt, the Asuras hate me, for they slaughter my disciples who come to them. (MatsP 25.47)
These fierce Dānavas desire to make him a non-Brāhmaṇa; indeed, this undertaking by them is in vain.
For even by such an act, his end might come here; for whom would the murder of a Brāhmaṇa not consume, even Indra himself?
Though unasked by him and summoned by his magical power, he slowly uttered a voice from within the belly.
He said to him: "By whom were you brought here? Tell me, my child, why you remain within my stomach."
Kaca said:
"By your grace, memory does not forsake me; I shall remember everything, exactly as it occurred.
Yet, let there be no depletion of my ascetic merit; therefore, I recall that [previous] suffering was even more terrible."
"O Kāvya, having slain, burnt, and ground you to powder, I have been given by the Asuras into the liquor for you.
Since you are present here, how can the Brahma-illusion and the Asura-illusion oppress me? (Matsya Purāṇa 25.51)
Śukra said:
"What dear thing shall I do for you today, my child? Kaca would not exist even at the cost of my life;
O Devayānī, Kaca could not be seen within me except by the bursting open of my belly."
Devayānī said:
"Two sorrows, like fires, would consume me: the destruction of Kaca and your own injury.
In the destruction of Kaca there is no peace for me; in the event of your injury, I am not able to live."
Śukra said:
"O son of Bṛhaspati, you have attained perfection since Devayānī, devoted to you, loves you.
Receive this life-restoring knowledge, lest Indra today take the form of a dwarf."
"No one else shall ever emerge alive from my belly, with the single exception of a Brāhmaṇa; therefore, acquire this knowledge. (Matsya Purāṇa 25.55)
"Having become my son, emerge from my womb; having pierced my side, give me life, O dear one.
Having obtained knowledge from your preceptor, become possessed of learning and look upon me with a righteous regard."
Śaunaka said:
Having acquired knowledge from his preceptor, the Brahmin emerged by bursting open his belly,
like the moon at the onset of night on a full-moon day, breaking through the white peak of the snowy mountain.
And seeing that heap of the Vedas fallen, Kaca then raised it up;
having obtained that perfected science and paid his respects, Kaca then spoke thus to his guru: matsyapurāṇe pañcaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ // MatsP_25.58 // (The twenty-fifth chapter in the Matsya Purāṇa)
Those who do not honor the Guru, the bestower of boons among boon-givers and the treasure-trove of all treasures—
who resides upon the forehead of the mountain of snow, radiant as the moon— those sinners go to worlds without support.

Śaunaka said: Having caused him to suffer the loss of consciousness and a terrible state of mind through the drinking of liquor and deception, and seeing Kaca likewise handsome yet thus consumed by the wine and deluded, [Śukra spoke]. *Matsya Purāṇa* 25.60.
Then the high-souled Uśanas Kāvya, rising up with great majesty and desiring to bring about their welfare,
spoke these words himself, having become apprehensive regarding the drinking of wine.
Śukra said:
"Whosoever among the Brāhmaṇas here, from this day forward, being of dull intellect, shall drink liquor out of delusion—
he shall be fallen from dharma, a slayer of a Brāhmaṇa, and he shall be censured in this world and in the next."

And let the virtuous Brahmins who have heard the teachings of their gurus, as well as all the gods and Daityas, listen to this boundary and limit established by me for the entire world according to the dharma of the Brahmins. (Matsya Purāṇa 25.63)
Śaunaka said: Having spoken thus, that one of immeasurable power, the treasury of the treasuries of asceticism,
summoned those Dānavas of hidden intellect and addressed these words to them.
Śukra said:
"I tell you, O Dānavas, you are fools! Kaca shall dwell near me as my pupil;
having obtained the science of Saṃjīvanī from me, this Brāhmaṇa will become equal to me in power and one with Brahman."
Śaunaka said:
Having resided in the presence of his guru for a thousand years,
Kaca, being granted permission, desired to go to the abode of the gods.
Matsya Purāṇa 26:
Śaunaka said: Then, when he had completed his vow and was dismissed by his preceptor, [he departed].
As he was setting out for the abode of the thirty gods, Devayānī spoke this to him.
Devayānī said:
"O grandson of the seer Aṅgiras, you shine by virtue of your conduct, your lineage, your learning, your austerity, and your self-restraint."
Just as the highly illustrious seer Aṅgiras is honored by my father,
so too is Bṛhaspati even more honored and worthy of worship by me.
Knowing this, O one whose wealth is asceticism, understand what I say:
how I shall conduct myself toward you while you are established in your vow and endowed with its observances.
"Having completed my studies, you ought not to abandon me, your devotee;
take my hand according to the rite, preceded by the sacred mantras."
Kaca said:
"O lady of faultless limbs, just as the Blessed One is worthy of worship and honor for me as my father,
so too are you considered most worthy of worship."
"O blessed lady, you are dearer to the high-souled Bhārgava than his own life;
as the daughter of my preceptor, you are always worthy of my worship according to dharma."
O Devayānī, just as my guru Śukra is always to be honored by you as your father, so too are you; therefore, you ought not to speak to me in this manner.
Devayānī said:
"The son of my preceptor’s son is my [son], but you are not the son of my father;
therefore, O best of the twice-born, you are both to be honored and worshipped by me as well."
But while you, Kaca, were being struck down by the Asuras again and again, remember for yourself that affection which I felt for you from that time forward. (Matsya Purāṇa 26.10)
"You know my friendship, my affection, and my supreme devotion toward you.
O knower of dharma, it does not behove you to abandon me, your innocent devotee."
Kaca said:
"O lady of auspicious vows, you are enjoining me to a task that is not my duty;
be gracious to me, O fair-browed one, for you, O auspicious one, are more venerable than my preceptor."
"O large-eyed one, O lady with a face like the moon, wherever you have dwelt,
there I have dwelt within the womb of Kāvya, O auspicious and beautiful woman."
"O fair-faced one, you are my sister by dharma; do not speak thus.
O blessed lady, I have dwelt in happiness, and no resentment exists within me. (Matsya Purāṇa 26.14)
I take my leave of you; I shall depart. May there be auspiciousness for me on the road. Without violating dharma, I should be remembered during your conversations.
Always remaining vigilant and diligent, honor my preceptor.
Devayānī said:

"Since you were slain by the Daityas and protected by me with the thought that you were my husband, if you now reject me according to dharma for the sake of dharma, desire, or wealth, [you will incur sin]. (Matsya Purāṇa 26.16)
"Therefore, O Kaca, this knowledge of yours shall not attain perfection."
Kacha said:
"Considering her to be the daughter of my preceptor, I shall not reject her out of any sense of fault;
moreover, having been permitted by my preceptor, curse me as you wish."
O Devayānī, O auspicious one, since I am proclaiming the dharma of the seers,
I am not worthy of being cursed by you today, whether out of desire or according to dharma.
Therefore, that desire of yours will not come to pass;
no son of a seer shall ever take your hand in marriage.
"My knowledge will not bear fruit for you," she said, "but it shall bear fruit for whomever I teach. (Matsya Purāṇa 26.21)
Śaunaka said:
Having spoken thus to Devayānī, O best of kings, Kaca, that most excellent of the twice-born, then departed swiftly for the abode of the lord of the gods. *Matsya Purāṇa* 26.22.

Seeing him arrive, the gods, led by Indra, honored Bṛhaspati and spoke thus to Kaca with joyful hearts: matsyapurāṇa 26.23.1–10: bṛhaspate prāptavānasi kacaṃ śīghraṃ tvamātmajam / kaccinna vidyayā hīnaḥ kaccinmukto 'si pāśataḥ // MatsP_26.23.1 // kaccinna vidyayā hīnaḥ kaccinna ca parābhavaḥ / kaccinna te parikleśo viphalo brahmavittama // MatsP_26.23.2 // bṛhaspatiruvāca: na vidyayā hīnaḥ kaca na ca mukto 'smi pāśataḥ / na me vidyāphalaṃ hīnaṃ na ca kleśaḥ parābhavaḥ // MatsP_26.23.3 // devā ūcuḥ: kathaṃ na vidyayā hīnaḥ kathaṃ mukto 'si pāśataḥ / kathaṃ na vidyāphalahīnaḥ kathaṃ kleśo na vai vṛthā // MatsP_26.23.4 // bṛhaspatiruvāca: vidyāprabhāvātkaco 'yaṃ punarjīvita eva ca / muktaḥ pāśādahaṃ cāpi vidyāyāḥ prabhāvataḥ // MatsP_26.23.5 // devā ūcuḥ: kenaiva vidyāprabhāveṇa kacaḥ punarjīvitaḥ / kasya vidyāprabhāveṇa tvaṃ muktaḥ pāśato bhṛśam // MatsP_26.23.6 // bṛhaspatiruvāca: śukreṇa vidyā dattaiṣā kacasyaiva mahātmanā / mayā caiva pradattaiṣā tena mukto 'smi pāśataḥ // MatsP_26.23.7 // devā ūcuḥ: aho vidyāmayaṃ tattvamaho vidyāprabhāvitam / aho vidyāprabhāvo 'yamaho vidyāparākramaḥ // MatsP_26.23.8 // bṛhaspatiruvāca: vidyāṃ yūyaṃ ca deveśāḥ samprāpya tridaśeśvarāḥ / asurāṇāṃ vadhaṃ kṛtvā svasthāneṣu nivatsyatha // MatsP_26.23.9 // devā ūcuḥ: vayaṃ vidyāṃ samprāpsyāmaḥ kenaiva vidhinā guro / vidyāprabhāvaṃ ca vayaṃ jñātumicchāmahe bhṛśam // MatsP_26.23.10 //
The gods said:
"O Kaca, you have performed a great and wonderful deed for our benefit;
your fame shall not perish, and you shall partake in a share [of the sacrificial offerings]. (Matsya Purāṇa 26.24)
Matsya Purāṇa 27:
Śaunaka said:
When Kaca had completed his studies and returned, the inhabitants of heaven were filled with joy.
O bull of the Bharatas, having obtained that lore from Kaca, she was fulfilled in her purpose.
Then, having all come together, they spoke to Śatakratu:
"The time for your valor has now arrived; slay the enemies, O Purandara! (Matsya Purāṇa 27.2)
Thus addressed by those thirty gods, Maghavan then said, "So be it," and proceeded; he beheld women in the forest.
While the maidens were playing in the forest that resembled Caitraratha,
he became the wind and blew away all their garments, mixing them together.
Then, having emerged from that water, those maidens together took up their garments many times over, each according to its original place.
Then Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, unaware of the transgression, took up the dwelling of Devayānī.
Then, O king of kings, a mutual conflict arose there between Devayānī and Śarmiṣṭhā on that account.
Devayānī said:
"O Asura, why do you seize my garment, having become my disciple?
Since you are devoid of proper conduct, no good shall come to you."
Śarmiṣṭhā said:
"Whether sitting or lying down, your father constantly praises and questions my father, remaining humble and well-disciplined like one of low station. (Matsya Purāṇa 27.9)
"You are the daughter of one who begs, praises, and accepts;
I am the daughter of one who is praised, gives, and does not accept. (Matsya Purāṇa 27.10)
"O mendicant woman, why are you angry with one who is armed while you are unarmed?
You shall find no one to fight you back, for I do not even count you. (Matsya Purāṇa 27.11)
Śaunaka said: Then Śarmiṣṭhā, having cast Devayānī— who was filled with astonishment and clinging to her garment—
into a well, entered her own city.
Thinking, "She hates me," Śarmiṣṭhā, having made a wicked resolve and overcome by the force of her anger, departed from that place without looking back. (Matsya Purāṇa 27.13)
Then Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa, arrived at that place;
his draft animals were exhausted, he was weary in appearance, thirsty, and seeking game.
For while looking at the waterless watering place, the son of Nahuṣa beheld that maiden there, blazing like a flame of fire. (Matsya Purāṇa 27.15)
Upon seeing that maiden who possessed the complexion of an immortal, that best of kings questioned her,
consoling her with most beautiful and gentle words.
Who are you, O lady with the beautiful face, dark-complexioned and adorned with well-polished jeweled earrings?
Why do you meditate so intensely for such a long time, and why do you sigh in distress?
"And how did you fall into this well covered with creepers and grass?
Whose daughter are you? Tell me everything, O slender-waisted one."
Devayānī said:
"I am the daughter of that Śukra who, by means of his secret knowledge, raises up the Daityas slain by the gods; you surely do not recognize me."
"O King, here is my right hand, with its copper-colored nails and fingers;
take hold of it and lift me up, for you are considered by me to be of noble birth. (Matsya Purāṇa 27.20)
I know you to be peaceful, heroic, and illustrious;
therefore, it behooves you to lift me up from this well into which I have fallen.
Śaunaka said: Then,
having recognized her as that very Brahmin woman, the son of Nahuṣa took her by the right hand and lifted her up from the pit.
Having swiftly lifted her from that well, O lord of men,
and having taken leave of the fair-hipped woman, Yayāti departed for his own city.
When that son of Nahuṣa had departed, the censured Devayānī, tormented by grief, spoke again to Ghūrṇikā who had returned. (Matsya Purāṇa 27.24)
Devayānī said:
"Ghūrṇikā, go quickly and tell my father everything;
I shall not enter the city of Vṛṣaparvan now. (Matsya Purāṇa 27.25)
Śaunaka said:
Having gone quickly to the palace of the Asura Ghūrṇika, she saw Kāvya and, trembling and nearly senseless, spoke these words. (Matsya Purāṇa 27.26)
And the illustrious Devayānī declared, "O man of great wisdom, she has been struck down in the forest by Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan. (Matsya Purāṇa 27.27)
Having heard that his daughter had been struck down by Śarmiṣṭhā,
Kāvya then went out in haste from his sorrow, searching for his daughter in the forest.

Seeing his daughter Devayānī in the penance grove, Kāvya embraced her with both arms and, being distressed, spoke these words: mānuṣeṇa śarīreṇa saṃyuktāsi sutena me / kasmāt tvam abhiśaptāsi kena vāsi vinākṛtā // MatsP_27.30 // "You are endowed with a human body, my daughter; why have you been cursed, or by whom have you been deprived? devayāny uvāca: pitā me bhagavān kāvyaḥ śrutaś caiva mahātapāḥ / sa yadāha tad evāham avaimi na tad anyathā // MatsP_27.31 // Devayānī said: "My father is the venerable Kāvya, renowned and of great ascetic power; whatever he has said, that very thing I know to be so, and not otherwise. yājñavalkya uvāca: tataḥ śrutvā tu tadvākyaṃ devayānyā prabhāṣitam / uvāca vacanaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ kanyām āmantrya śukrajaḥ // MatsP_27.32 // Yājñavalkya said: Then, having heard those words spoken by Devayānī, the son of Śukra addressed the maiden and spoke these gentle words: devayāni nibodha tvaṃ yat tvāṃ vakṣyāmi tat sutam / na te 'nyathā tad bhavitā tat tathā kartum arhasi // MatsP_27.33 // "O Devayānī, listen to what I shall say to you, my daughter; it shall not be otherwise, and you ought to act accordingly. devayāny uvāca: brūhi tāta yathābhūtaṃ śrotum icchāmi te vacaḥ / na te 'nyathā hi tad bhāvi tat tathā kartum arhasi // MatsP_27.34 // Devayānī said: "Speak, O father, according to the truth; I wish to hear your word. For it shall not be otherwise, and you ought to act so that it becomes so. śukra uvāca: yājñavalkya uvāca: śṛṇu putrike yena tvaṃ śaptāsi dvijasattama / yājñavalkya uvāca: yenāsi śaptā subhage yājñavalkyaṃ tam uddiśan // MatsP_27.35 // Śukra said: Yājñavalkya said: Listen, my daughter, as to who that best of the twice-born is by whom you were cursed. Yājñavalkya said: [He cursed] Yājñavalkya, pointing him out, O fortunate one, because of whom you were cursed. devayāny uvāca: yājñavalkyaṃ na jānāmi śaptaṃ kenāpi hetunā / yājñavalkya uvāca: devayāni nibodha tvaṃ yājñavalkyaṃ tam uddiśan // MatsP_27.36 // Devayānī said: "I do not know Yājñavalkya, nor for what reason he was cursed. Yājñavalkya said: "O Devayānī, understand that it was directed toward Yājñavalkya. devayāny uvāca: yājñavalkyaṃ na jānāmi śaptaṃ kenāpi hetunā / yājñavalkya uvāca: devayāni nibodha tvaṃ yājñavalkyaṃ tam uddiśan // MatsP_27.37 // Devayānī said: "I do not know Yājñavalkya, nor for what reason he was cursed. Yājñavalkya said: "O Devayānī, understand that it was directed toward Yājñavalkya. devayāny uvā
"All people experience suffering and happiness according to their own faults;
I believe you have committed some misdeed, for which this atonement has been made."
Devayānī said:
"Whether there be atonement or not, listen attentively to what I have been told by Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan. (Matsya Purāṇa 27.31)
"This is indeed true," she said; "I am a singer for the Daityas, for Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, tells me so."
With eyes intensely red with anger, she spoke words that were sharp and harsh:
"You are the daughter of one who praises, begs, and accepts! (Matsya Purāṇa 27.33)
"I have heard you being praised while giving and not receiving," Śarmiṣṭhā,
the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, then said to me,
her eyes bloodshot with anger and her face full of pride. (Matsya Purāṇa 27.34)
"O father, if I am to accept the daughter of one who praises me, I shall propitiate Śarmiṣṭhā"—thus indeed was my friend addressed by me. (Matsya Purāṇa 27.35)
Śukra said:
"O blessed lady, you are not the daughter of one who praises, nor of one who accepts praise;
therefore, Devayānī, you are the daughter of him who is being praised."
Vṛṣaparvan alone knew that, as did Śakra and King Nahuṣa:
"The Brahman is inconceivable and free from duality; for such is my divine power."
Matsya Purāṇa 28:
Śukra said:
"The man who constantly endures the harsh words of others..."
O Devayānī, understand this: by him all this has been conquered.
He who restrains arisen anger like a horse is called a "driver" by the virtuous, not he who merely hangs onto the reins.
